selected_evidence.requirement: opsadmin account and supplied public key configured
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the account, locked password, correct ownership and permissions, exact key match, and ED25519 fingerprint before and after reboot.
Effective sshd policy requires publickey, disables password and challenge-response authentication, and the live server advertises only publickey authentication.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f; reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 0eb5ca4c-9fcf-4331-98d5-f638cb50447d, system state running, sshd active/enabled and listening, with the account, key, permissions, and key-only policy intact.

else

commands.command:
set -eu
probe=/tmp/opsadmin-ssh-auth-probe.$$
set +e
ssh -vv -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o IdentityFile=/dev/null opsadmin@"$NODE_IP" true >"$probe" 2>&1
rc=$?
set -e
grep -E 'Authentications that can continue:|Permission denied' "$probe"
grep -q 'Authentications that can continue: publickey' "$probe"
rm -f "$probe"
printf 'probe_exit=%s expected_without_matching_private_key=yes\n' "$rc"
